items.summary: Adding an inference replica creates capacity only after the new instance can serve requests. Between starting a process and generating a response, an LLM server may need to load weights, initialize GPU resources, compile kernels, capture...
items.content: Adding an inference replica creates capacity only after the new instance can serve requests. Between starting a process and generating a response, an LLM server may need to load weights, initialize GPU resources, compile kernels, capture execution graphs, and warm up the engine. Restarts, model switches, and scale-out can repeat this work. The community is addressing these costs at several levels. vLLM and SGLang are developing ways to reuse weights and initialized state.

items.content: When you deploy a model to a GPU endpoint, the smallest unit of GPU you can request is one whole accelerator. This constraint can cost you twice. Second, and less obvious, it makes every deployment come down to a choice of which full GPU to deploy to.

items.title: Taxonomy of agentic primitives in Amazon Quick
items.summary: As we built Amazon Quick, its agents grew from answering questions to taking actions, and the same primitives kept getting rebuilt under different names. This post shares the taxonomy we converged on — triggers, agents, capabilities, and learned context — found by decomposing agentic work into four plain questions: When, What, Who, and How.
items.content: Over the past year, as we built Amazon Quick, our agents went from answering questions to taking actions: scheduling meetings, running research, generating reports. As the system evolved, one problem kept resurfacing: there was no shared definition of the primitives that agentic work is built from. The same few ideas kept getting rebuilt under different names: an actor that does the work, a signal that starts it, a packaged procedure, and a memory that carries lessons forward.

items.content: An AI agent that updates a ticket or reads a customer record acts for a person, inside applications that person can reach. items.title: The post-quantum future of web privacy
items.summary: Cryptographic protocols like Privacy Pass help keep web sites safe from abuse while keeping their users private. This post looks at the quantum threat to these protocols, and some new post-quantum cryptography that may help close the gap.
items.content: The highest priorities for the transition to post-quantum cryptography are the basic building blocks of authenticated key-agreement protocols such as TLS. Without these building blocks in place, secure communication on the Internet will not be possible once cryptographically relevant quantum computers come online. However, today we rely on quantum-vulnerable cryptography for much more than TLS.

items.summary: A backdoor has been found hiding in the web server that runs Control Web Panel (CWP), a free panel for managing Linux hosting servers, researchers at QiAnXin's XLab said this week. Installing it takes root access, so the attackers must already control the server.

items.content: 신재생 에너지 전문기업 인코어드(Encored)는 재생에너지 발전량 예측을 위해 고해상도 기상 시뮬레이션을 오픈소스 기상 모델 WRF로 수행하며, 온프레미스 클러스터 없이 AWS HPC 전용 인스턴스 위에서 운영하고 있습니다. 이 글은 AWS HPC 전용 인스턴스에서 WRF를 운영한 경험을 정리한 2부작 시리즈의 두 번째 글입니다. 1부에서 “어느 인스턴스를 몇 노드로 고를 것인가”를 다뤘다면, 2부의 질문은 하나입니다. 같은 인스턴스, 같은 vCPU 총량을 MPI 프로세스와 OpenMP 스레드로 어떻게 나눠 쓸 때 가장 빠른가? 직관과는 반대였습니다.
